confidence: Confidence is moderate. Most roles had only three tasks. B-roll Editing and Taste each had two scored tasks, and the third Taste task was for reference only. Each task had one scored attempt, so the results do not show how performance varies across attempts. These results apply to the Claude channel and its default reasoning setting.

avoid: Have a person make final Taste and B-roll choices for voiceovers. The model lost substantial points on both types of scored task.
Avoid assigning work that requires listening to the audio, such as identifying the language or checking for dialogue.
Have someone listen to clips with sound before adding the model's footage log to the library.
give: Use it to find specified shots in long footage and check timing cues. It will say when it cannot find a shot.
Use it to revise a timeline from notes. It asks first when a note is ambiguous. When the instructions are clear, tell it that it can proceed without asking again.
Use it for a first pass on Review and for draft subtitles on short voiceovers. Have a person review the results.

honesty:
No false claims were found. Evidence supported 104 claims and contradicted 0. Another 32 could not be verified. The model said when it had not listened to the recording and reported commands it ran outside the task directory on its own.

It handled 13 of 18 traps and marked 27 answerable items as uncertain. Those answers limit how useful the results are in practice. They did not count as false claims.
one_line: The overall score was 76.23 without speed and 76.17 with speed. The model passed 10 of 22 scored tasks. It was consistent at finding specified shots. It is worth trying on revisions with a clear scope and submits quickly. A person should take over when edits call for editorial judgment, listening to the audio, or choosing B-roll.

roles.text: The Footage Logging role score with speed was 72.31. It passed one of three tasks. It scored 96.43 without speed on the short-asset logging task (SORT2), where it marked the intended use of two assets as uncertain. The film-clip logging task (SORT3) asked it to log clips and identify spans of repeated footage. It found the repeated sections accurately. It did not listen to the audio, marked every dialogue check for clips with an audio track as uncertain, and failed to identify half the film titles.

The Shot Finding role score with speed was 90.82. It passed two of three tasks. The hardest task, FIND3, asked it to check two shots and one timing cue. It got all three items right. On the identification task (FIND2), it marked four film titles and one person as uncertain. It scored 72.62 without speed. Use it to find specified shots, and check its film and person identifications.

The Voiceover Editing role score with speed was 94.72. It passed two of three tasks. On the medium-difficulty task with natural speech (VO2), it earned full marks without speed and handled restarts, tangents, and long pauses correctly. On the difficult task with two recordings (VO3), it spotted a mismatch but marked its conclusion as uncertain. The grader gave it no credit for handling that key trap. It also earned full marks without speed on the simple task (VO1). It kept the right sections and gave the correct reasons.

It failed both scored B-roll Editing tasks. CUT1 and CUT3 scored 28.00 and 28.57 without speed, respectively. It lost points on footage selection. Have a person make the final picks. On CUT3, the command working directory switched to a location outside the task directory. The model created, inspected, and deleted an empty folder there, then reported it on its own. The out-of-directory access was logged without a penalty.

With editing rules to consult, it followed the rules and all 20 choices matched the usable final cut. Without rules to consult, 8 of 15 choices matched. It scored only 6.67 without speed on that task. Based on this result, have a person make the final call on how to cut. The third task, which asked it to watch footage and choose clip in and out points, was for reference only and did not count toward the assessment.

The Review role score with speed was 83.82. It passed one of three tasks. On the hardest task (QC3), it found all the issues. It took 518.9 seconds and still scored 99.09 with speed. It passed on the strength of the content. On the simple task (QC1), which checked for black frames, white flashes, and watermarks, it missed one visual issue. Its report acknowledged that it had only spot-checked the four corners of the frame.

The Revisions role score with speed was 83.33. It passed two of three tasks. Check that it made the specific changes requested. On FIX3, it correctly identified the scope of the revision note. It earned full marks without speed. On the simple task with three clear notes (FIX1), it judged the instructions unclear and changed nothing. That cost it half the points.

The Subtitles role score with speed was 79.21. It passed only one of three tasks. On the simple voiceover subtitle task (SUB1), it scored 98.89 without speed, corrected proper names, and left unfinished sentences unfinished. On the subtitle placement task (SUB2), it mishandled differences between the transcript and the script. On the difficult original-audio subtitle task (SUB3), it got the language wrong, reused the reference transcript, and displayed the subtitles for too little of the speech. It scored 55.23 without speed.

working_style:
It submitted all 22 scored tasks without timeouts, late submissions, or re-dispatches. The median time from start to submission was 97.2 seconds, and the median number of tool calls was 13. It spent a median of 13.7 seconds checking its work after the last change to a deliverable. It usually wrapped up quickly.

It generated 405,884 output tokens across the scored tasks, including 290,327 reasoning tokens. The access channel records token usage. It does not affect scoring. The model relied on existing transcripts and volume curves for voiceovers and subtitles and said in its reports that it did not listen to the audio. This approach can produce incorrect edits or subtitles when the reference transcript differs from the recording.
